sources.entry: pymc - Probabilistic programming and Bayesian modeling in Python.

summary.one_liner: PyMC is a Python package for Bayesian statistical modeling, focused on MCMC sampling (including NUTS) and variational inference.
summary.what_it_does: PyMC (formerly PyMC3) lets you specify probabilistic models in Python using a concise syntax, for example x ~ N(0,1) becomes x = Normal('x',0,1). It provides MCMC samplers such as the No U-Turn Sampler and variational inference methods including ADVI and mini-batch ADVI for large datasets. Models are built on PyTensor, which supplies computation optimization, dynamic C or JAX compilation, NumPy-style broadcasting, and linear algebra operators. The README also shows a linear regression workflow covering prior predictive sampling, conditioning on data, posterior predictive sampling for new inputs, and interventions with pm.do. It supports transparent missing-value imputation.
use_cases: fitting regression models with uncertainty estimates
fast approximate posterior estimation with variational inference
simulating data from a prior or fitted model
handling missing values in a statistical model
causal what-if scenarios on model parameters
how_to_run: pip install pymc (see the installation guide linked in the README)
with pm.Model(coords=coords) as model: ... define priors and likelihood
notable: Uses the No U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) and ADVI variational inference, including mini-batch ADVI
Model syntax mirrors statistical notation, e.g. x ~ N(0,1)
Includes pm.do and pm.observe for interventions and conditioning on data
Formerly PyMC3; backed by NumFOCUS as a non-profit project
Has an ecosystem of packages built on it such as Bambi, CausalPy and PyMC-Marketing
